newsitem.title: USA: Calcol's Chinese license, venture in peril.
newsitem.headline: Calcol's Chinese license, venture in peril.

text.p: Calcol Inc, a Beechwood, Ohio, company seeking business opportunities in China, said Thursday there was "substantial likelihood" it may lose its business license and see its joint venture with a Chinese partner terminated.

It said in a statement that it recently received a notice of from its partner, Changbaisan Enterprises Co Ltd, about the actions the Chinese firm may take because of Calcol's failure to make a required $5.1 million additional investments in Shenzhen-Calcol Changbaishan Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, their joint venture.
Calcol said it invested $900,000 in the venture, while Changbaishan, which is based in China's southern city of Shenzehen, had put up $5.0 million.
It said it and Calcol Hazak LLC, to which it transferred its 50 percent interest in the venture, had been seeking a buyer for the stake or alternative financing.
But efforts have been fruitless so far, Calcol said.
"We're trying various investment sources," said David Orlean, a Calcol official, in a phone interview. He said there was always a chance funds may be obtained, but did not give details.
Calcol said in the statement it expects liquidation of the joint venture assets if its business license was revoked. It added it may be subject to penalties for breach of contract.

Calcol said it also received notice from another Chinese partner, China National Food Industry Group Co, of Beijing, that it was in default of an obligation to make an additional $3.6 million bottling equipment investment in a soft-drink joint venture, Sanhe Mei-le Soft Drinks Co.
In addition, it had not made a required $3.2 million investment in the venture, it said.
In the venture, it said it had had invested $1.762 million while the Chinese government had invested $1.44 million and had made a commmitted for an additional $560,000.

Calcol said it has been in discussions with various financing sources, including Asia-based sources, to fund the venture's soft-drink project and for the possible sale of its stake. It said there can be no assurance that any sort of financing or sale will be completed.

Its business license with the Sanhe Mei-le Soft Drinks Co Ltd has been extended until June 30 pending results of financing talks. If it is unable to raise funds, it said the license may be suspeended or revoked and assets of the venture may be liquidated.
